key_insight: The paper shows that likelihood alone is not enough to detect whether a token or example came from pretraining data in large language models. By correcting prediction loss with predictive entropy, the detector uses an inclined decision boundary that better separates true members from highly predictable non-members.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of identifying pretraining data in LLMs when high likelihood can come from either memorization or strong generalization, causing likelihood-only methods to produce false positives.
method: Model the detection problem in the joint space of prediction loss and predictive entropy.
Replace a horizontal likelihood threshold with an inclined boundary that compares loss against entropy.
Use entropy correction to reduce confusion between memorized training samples and naturally predictable inputs.
impact: This improves the reliability of data membership detection for large language models. For practitioners, it offers a more robust way to audit training data, study memorization, and assess privacy or leakage risks.
visual_elements: 2D scatter plot of prediction loss vs. predictive entropy with horizontal vs. inclined decision boundaries
Side-by-side comparison of 'member' and 'non-member' examples showing where likelihood-only methods fail
Flow diagram of the entropy-corrected detection pipeline
Icon set representing memorization, generalization, and privacy leakage
paper_title: Detecting Pretraining Data in Large Language Models from a Free-Energy Perspective
paper_authors: Chenye Ke, Zirui Liu, Qi Liu, Yan Zhuang, Jintao Zhang
